snippet.text: Q ^ (-(1/2 + h) - 1) / Q ^ (-2*(1/2 + h) - 1/2) = Q ^ h — the diffusive-to-inertial ratio, whose numerator exponent -A - 1 carries the same factor q^(-1) = 1/ℓ_r², but a different identity

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: No Lean counterpart was found. No declaration stating either rate identity was found. Scaling.lean, the file that formalizes exactly this family of scale counts, defines radialLength q = q^(1/2) and axialLength q h = q^(1/2 - h) and coreVelocity q h = q^(-(1/2+h)), but states only the two Reynolds products; it contains nothing of the form q^(-A)/ℓ_z = q^(-1) or 1/ℓ_r² = q^(-1), and axialLength is used nowhere else in NavierStokes/ outside core_axial_reynolds. Both equalities are one-line rpow arithmetic from those three definitions (-(1/2+h) - (1/2-h) = -1 and -2·(1/2) = -1), so this is unstated rather than contradicted. For the first rate there is less: no declaration giving a scale for |u_r^(0)| was found, so |u_r^(0)|/ℓ_r = O(q^(-1)) has no counterpart at all. The nearest stated fact is normalized_viscosity, a different ratio.
